title: Operational contracts for coordinated limited release (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational contract template for coordinating small/limited releases (phased adoption, gated launches, partner pilots) that require cross-functional alignment between Product, Eng (SRE & Serving), Solutions/SE, and Customer Success. Aim: reduce ambiguity about who watches what, what signals gate growth, and how to run fast safe rollouts for LLM features.

Scope and intent:
- Applicability: new model variants, prompt changes, routing/policy adjustments, and UI features that alter inference patterns.
- Not for: emergency hotfixes (follow incident runbook) or long-term A/B experiments managed by growth.

High-level contract (one-line commitments):
- Product: defines hypothesis, user cohorts, and success metrics.
- SRE/Serving: commits to observability hooks, automated traffic shaping, and latency/error SLO monitoring for rollout phases.
- Solutions/CS: provides contact list, pilot participant coordination, and UX acceptance feedback.
- Security/Compliance: signs off on data handling for pilot cohorts before activation.

Roles & responsibilities (operational owners):
- Release Lead (Product) - owner of rollout decision and cadence. (example: Asha Patel)
- Runtime Owner (Serving/Infra) - ensures model variant deployed, autoscaling rules in place, KV cache priming strategy, and provides perf dashboard links. (Marcus Li)
- SRE Oncall - watches infra-level metrics and can trigger immediate throughput controls.
- Evaluation Lead (Applied ML) - tracks quality regressions on golden promptset. (Rina Gomez)
- CS/Partner Lead - manages participant communication and collects qualitative feedback.

Gating signals (example thresholds) - these are minimum; teams can tighten:
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency increase <= 15% relative to baseline sustained for 10m.
- Error rate: user-facing errors (generation timeouts/invalid outputs) <= 0.5% absolute increase over baseline across cohort.
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens not exceed forecast by more than 25% in first 24h.
- Quality: automated eval score on golden prompts not degrade by > 3 points (absolute) or fail regression tests.
- Availability: no sustained region-wide capacity falls or >1% request failures due to infra scaling for more than 5m.
- User-level signals: NPS or satisfaction survey score drop > 10 points (pilot-level) triggers pause.

Phase plan (example 4-step):
- Phase 0 - Dry run (internal): route 0.1% internal traffic, smoke checks, priming. Duration 2–6 hours.
- Phase 1 - Partner pilot: 1–5% of selected partner cohort or internal beta customers. Duration 24–72 hours.
- Phase 2 - Broad limited: 5–25% of broader cohort segmented by geography/device. Duration 3–7 days.
- Phase 3 - General availability: open to all; prepare automated rollback policies in place.

Traffic allocation and routing details (ops knobs):
- Can route by traffic-weights at the API gateway or feature-flag service. Prefer gateway for hard isolation.
- Use session stickiness only if feature is stateful; otherwise prefer request-level routing.
- Provide explicit fallthrough: if capacity constraint triggers, route to last-stable model variant.

Automated guards and runbook triggers:
- Auto-scale lock: if 95th latency > threshold AND error rate rising, set new requests to fallback model for 5 minutes and escalate.
- Error budget gating: if incident causes > X% of error budget burn in 1h, immediately pause rollout.
- Canary heartbeat: a scheduled synthetic traffic job that runs golden prompts every 5m and posts to the rollout dashboard. Failing 3 consecutive hearts triggers alert.

Rollback criteria (immediate vs monitored):
- Immediate (auto or manual): critical customer-impacting failures (data leak, catastrophic hallucination causing regulatory risk, region outage).
- Monitored (requires team decision): sustained SLA regressions, cost runaway, or quality regression beyond agreed tolerance.

Communication protocol during rollout:
- Slack channel: #rollout-<feature>-<date> (must be created by Release Lead before Phase 0). All alerts should post there.
- Twice-daily async status updates during partner pilot windows unless an alert fires.
- Post-mortem within 3 business days for any rollback or >P1 incident.

Observability checklist (must exist before Phase 1):
- Dashboard links: latency by region & model, error breakdown, cost-per-token by model, golden prompt regression curve.
- Tracing: end-to-end request IDs surfaced to CS for investigating user tickets.
- Logs: structured model selection logs, routing decisions, and fallback triggers.
- Eval harness: automated re-eval of golden set and top-k failure samples pushed to slack.

Experiment measurement (minimal viable signal):
- Primary metric (product-defined): e.g., completion usefulness score or task success rate.
- Safety metrics: hallucination incidents flagged per 10k requests, sensitive content hits.
- Latency & cost: token latency P95, cost per 1k tokens.
- Qualitative: top-5 customer feedback snippets per cohort.

Hazard log (things to watch for) - quick notes:
- Cold cache behavior: initial token cost & latency spike when priming occurs. Plan for warm-up synthetic traffic.
- Tokenization edge-cases: different clients sending unusual sequence lengths.
- Model deterministic drift: A/B-ish differences due to temperature/seeding changes. Explicitly log model seed/config.
- Billing surprises from third-party models or cross-region egress.

Checklist before Phase 0 (go/no-go):
- [ ] Product hypothesis & cohort list documented
- [ ] Performance dashboard wired and smoke-tested
- [ ] Synthetic heartbeats running and passing at baseline
- [ ] Release channel created and shared with oncall teams
- [ ] Fallback model verified and test-invoked
- [ ] Customer communication template approved by CS
- [ ] Security sign-off for data flow for pilot cohort

Emergency contact matrix:
- Release Lead (Product): asha.patel@redwood.ai, +1-555-0113
- Runtime Owner (Serving): marcus.li@redwood.ai, +1-555-0120
- SRE Pager: #sre-oncall (primary)
- Applied ML Eval Lead: rina.gomez@redwood.ai

Open questions and unresolved decisions (work-in-progress):
- What exact percentage thresholds should auto-pause use for small vs large customers?
- How to reconcile cost anomalies for multi-tenant vs dedicated workloads in the same trial?
- Do we permit opt-in sticky sessions for latency-sensitive partners? (product/SRE tradeoff)

Next steps and owners:
- Action: finalize gating thresholds for two canonical experiment types (low-risk UI tweak, high-risk model change). Owner: Release Lead. Due: 2024-11-12.
- Action: add auto-pause implementation PR to serving runtime repo and link. Owner: Runtime Owner. Due: 2024-11-19.
- Action: craft pilot customer notice template and share with CS. Owner: CS Lead. Due: 2024-11-08.

Notes to self / friction anecdotes (informal):
- partner pilots often fail because partner billing alignment wasn't squared; embed billing contact in pilot kickoff.
- early experiments forget to include negative-control prompts; keep a small fixed negative set to detect stealth regressions.

Appendix: quick rollout decision flow (one-pager):
1) Phase readiness check (dashboard up, heartbeats green) -> 2) Start Phase 0 -> 3) Evaluate 6h signals -> 4) If green, move to Phase 1 and notify partners -> 5) If any gating signal tripped, pause and initiate triage meeting within 30m -> 6) Triage outcome: rollback vs iterate & resume.

End of draft.

-- Asha
